content.title: About
content.content: Light mayonnaise-type salad dressing is a creamy vinaigrette made from vegetable oils, egg yolks, vinegar and spices. It offers a smooth texture, mild flavor and considerably fewer calories than traditional mayonnaise.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The formula usually relies on rapeseed or sunflower oil, making it healthier than saturated‑fat‑rich versions.
Light versions often reduce the amount of egg or use egg substitutes, lowering cholesterol content.
Vinegar and lemon juice give the dressing its characteristic light tang.
Many flavor variations exist: herb, garlic, mustard, or spice‑infused versions.
It is a popular choice in diet‑focused meals and fast‑service restaurant menus.

items.title: Low calorie content
items.content: Compared with regular mayonnaise, the light dressing provides roughly two‑to‑three times fewer calories, helping with energy balance.

items.title: Rich in monounsaturated fats
items.content: The vegetable oils supply monounsaturated fatty acids that support cardiovascular health.

items.title: Source of vitamin E
items.content: The oils are a good source of vitamin E, an antioxidant that protects cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: May contain probiotics (in some formulations)
items.content: If fermented vinegar is used, the dressing can contribute to a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Improves absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins
items.content: A small amount of fat aids the body in absorbing vitamins A, D, E and K from vegetables served with the dressing.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Traditional recipes contain egg yolks, which can trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Some brands add noticeable amounts of salt; people monitoring blood pressure should check the sodium level.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: To extend shelf life, preservatives may be used, which can be problematic for those with sensitivities to food additives.

items.title: Possible trans fats (rare)
items.content: If partially hydrogenated oil is present, trans fats may be included, which are detrimental to heart health.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: The dressing works well on salads, vegetable sticks, sandwiches and wraps. It can also serve as a base for marinades, grill sauces, or a light herb dip.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store refrigerated at 2 °C–5 °C. After opening, consume within 7‑10 days. Do not freeze, as the texture may separate.
